headline: Moving a component into its own module is free: the primitives and the JSX that uses them travel together, folding still sees both, and next-yak lands within the run-to-run spread of the single-file case.

microbench.why: This is the Example `tabs` with its styled primitives moved into an imported `parts.tsx`. `next-yak` renders at 85,900 against 80,800 in the single-file case — a gap the wrong way round for a boundary penalty, and inside the spread either way — because `parts.tsx` holds the declarations and their JSX use sites together, and `fold_jsx_usages` needs both in one module rather than in the entry. `vanilla` at 153,000 and `stylex-layers` at 142,000 lead exactly as they do on `tabs`. The only thing that genuinely crosses a boundary here is the `styled(Tabs)` wrapper, one component out of sixteen elements, which is why the case reads as a null result.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-css` at 675 req/s and `vanilla` at 665 lead, and every lane finishes within a few percent of its `tabs` figure. A module boundary that carries declarations and use sites together costs nothing under load either.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

attribution.why: `vanilla` at 1.34 ms and `stylex-layers` at 1.45 ms hold the floor. `next-yak` at 2.09 ms sits below the 2.24 ms it spends on `tabs`, and its 0.833 ms of lib self-time is the same dynamic-prop closure blocking the fold, not a cost of the import. Every lane lands within a few percent of its single-file result.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: Six lanes between 44.8 ms and 47.7 ms, matching `tabs` lane for lane. `goober` at 187 ms and `styled-components` at 192 ms rebuild their sheets, as they do everywhere.

inp.why: Ten lanes answer between 6.6 ms and 7.8 ms. `panda-props` at 25.7 ms and `emotion` at 25.8 ms re-derive the state matrix when a tab changes.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Eight lanes mount between 87.9 ms and 96.4 ms, again matching `tabs`. The sheet-building lanes need 189 ms to 214 ms.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, 0.847 ms to 1.02 ms for twelve lanes and 1.64 ms to 1.91 ms for the three that inject their sheet at render.

payload.why: Byte for byte the same page as `tabs`: `vanilla` and `next-yak-css-nofold` at 2,690 gz B, `next-yak` at 3,512 B against 3,511 B. Splitting a component into its own module changes nothing that reaches the browser.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: `stylex-layers` at 29.3 ms, `stylex` at 29.3 ms and `vanilla` at 29.6 ms hold their line, and `next-yak` at 66.1 ms tracks the 66.3 ms it posts on `tabs`. The slope comes from the blocked fold inside the Tab component, not from the file layout.

crossCase: This is the Example `tabs` shown above with the styled primitives moved into an imported `parts.tsx`, and nothing measurable changes. Read it against the Example `multifile-shop`, which asks the other half of the question: there the primitives ship for a different module's JSX to use, `fold_jsx_usages` never sees a declaration and its use site together, and `next-yak` gives up 43% of its throughput. Moving a whole component across a file is free; shipping primitives for someone else to use is not.
